## Context / Problem
Automated bug filers can spam duplicates, file on single flakes, or silently break when create args/gates change (0e15/376d class: gate changes broke automated surfaces). The audit surface is the THREE existing filers — no new filer is built; this ticket HARDENS what exists and documents the contract for future filers: the heartbeat-alert filer (scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:197) and the binding-drift-alert filer (cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:350) — canary_bridge.py has exactly these two create sites, verified by inventory —, plus `_file_conflict_bug_ticket` in the reconciler applier (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:135, called at :522), which today files one bug per unresolved (local, Jira) conflict with no dedup key, no template contract, and no empty-detail abort.

## Approach
Per OSS practice (PyTorch DISABLED-test bot, Flutter flake bot, Sentry fingerprinting, Alertmanager 'for:'): dedup via a stable per-check TAG searched with has-tag (one open ticket per check); file only after N>=2 consecutive reds; max one accumulation comment/day; templated body (check name, first-red time, run URL, failing-output tail, workflow path) with abort-if-empty-detail; recovery comment on green with close left to agents is documented in the CONTRACT as the default for future filers whose bugs carry investigation value; it is NOT retrofitted anywhere in this ticket. The two canary_bridge filers ALREADY auto-close their alert ticket on green via `rebar transition open closed --force-close` (cmd_heartbeat_alert ~:247-262, cmd_binding_drift_alert ~:398-410) — that existing recovery contract is KEPT AS-IS (pure state alerts, nothing to investigate once green); the audit records this divergence and its rationale in the table rather than retrofitting agent-close onto them. Pattern elements apply per-site by SEMANTIC FIT, recorded in the audit table: the N>=2 consecutive-red threshold applies only where a derivable red/green run signal exists: the HEARTBEAT filer only — its stale check fails the canary run (the 'Fail job on stale' step), so the workflow's previous run conclusion carries the signal. The BINDING-DRIFT filer gets NO threshold, with rationale recorded: its oracle never fails the run (conclusion carries no drift signal), and drift is PERSISTENT state, not a flake — it cannot self-heal between runs, so first-observation filing is correct and dedup + daily accumulation already bound spam; the conflict filer has no cycle semantics, so it gets dedup (stable tag derived from the conflict identity: local id + jira key), template, abort-if-empty, and detected_by — not the threshold. CONSECUTIVE-RED STATE STORE: no new state store — the workflow's own run history is the durable state. On red, the filer queries the same workflow's previous completed run conclusion (gh api repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/{file}/runs?status=completed&per_page=2, excluding the current run); previous-also-red => threshold met; previous-green-or-absent => first red, no ticket. Dedup search runs FIRST: an existing open tagged ticket always takes the accumulate-comment path regardless of threshold. ACCUMULATION DEDUP ('max one accumulation comment/day'): derived from the target ticket's OWN comment history — the accumulation comment opens with a stable marker line; the filer reads the ticket (rebar show --output json), finds the newest marker-bearing comment, and skips if it is <24h old. The ticket store IS the durable state; no new store, and the */20 cron cannot spam. First-red time in the template = the previous red run's timestamp. WORKFLOW THREADING (scope): the consuming alert steps in .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml today pass only STALE/RUN_URL/DRIFT_* env; the heartbeat alert step's run-history query additionally needs GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (already used by other steps in that workflow), the repo (github.repository), and the workflow file id (the literal filename) threaded as step env — enumerated as workflow edits in scope, heartbeat step only. The contract doc records the same recipe for future filers with run-conclusion signals. LIFECYCLE: green with no open tagged ticket (single flake that never crossed the threshold) => recovery path no-ops on the empty has-tag search — stated as an invariant and unit-tested. USER-REQUIRED ADDITIONS: (a) audit ALL existing auto-bug-creation sites and retrofit the fitting pattern elements; (b) document the bug-creation contract for automation — exact rebar create args, exit codes, dedup search command, REBAR_DETECTED_BY env var — so auto-filers always fire a well-formed create.

## Scope
- canary/heartbeat/binding-drift filer scripts or workflow logic (coordinate with Tier-3 migration child if concurrent)
- src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py `_file_conflict_bug_ticket`: dedup tag + template + abort-if-empty + detected_by (no threshold — no red/green cycle)
- docs: bug-creation contract page
- audit table of every auto-file site in the change description, with a per-site row: which pattern elements apply and why

## Testing
Heartbeat-filer unit tests: first red -> no ticket; second consecutive red -> one ticket with template fields; third red same day -> accumulation comment, not a new ticket; second accumulation within 24h -> skipped (marker-line dedup); green with open ticket -> existing auto-close path preserved (transition open closed --force-close, unchanged); green with NO open ticket -> no-op, exit 0; empty detail -> abort with loud log, no hollow ticket; previous-run query failure -> treated as first red (fail toward not filing, loud log). Binding-drift tests: first observed drift -> one ticket (no threshold, rationale in table); repeat drift -> accumulation not duplicate; green -> existing auto-close preserved. Conflict-filer tests: same conflict twice -> one ticket + one accumulation comment; distinct conflicts -> distinct tickets; empty conflict detail -> abort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All three audited auto-file sites use the fitting dedup+template pattern elements (audit table enumerates sites x elements with rationale, including the kept auto-close divergence and the binding-drift no-threshold rationale).
- [ ] Heartbeat consecutive-red threshold implemented via workflow run-history query; no new state store introduced; single flake files nothing.
- [ ] Bug-creation contract documented and referenced by every filer.
- [ ] Filer behavior covered by the unit tests above, including the green-with-no-ticket no-op and the query-failure arm.
- [ ] detected_by stamped by all automated filers (env var from the detected-by child).
